ops.title: Embedded SPA with committed placeholder — go build green without web toolchain
ops.body:
# Embedded SPA: committed placeholder keeps go build green without a web toolchain

`internal/web` mirrors cc-present's embed pattern exactly (cc-present `internal/web/embed.go`):

- `embed.go` does `//go:embed all:dist` and exposes `Dist() fs.FS` rooted at `dist/`.
- `dist/index.html` is a **committed placeholder** shell, so `go build ./...` succeeds on a clean tree that never ran npm/bun. `go:embed` fails the build if `dist` is empty — the placeholder is what keeps CI and fresh clones compiling.
- `.gitignore` carries `/internal/web/dist/*` with `!/internal/web/dist/index.html`, so a real web build's hashed artifacts never enter version control; only index.html (placeholder or built) is committed.

Serving: `runtime/server.go` mounts `sse.StaticHandler(web.Dist())` on the catch-all `/` of the daemon's mux. Go's pattern mux keeps `/events` and `/api/*` ahead of it, and cc-interact's `startHTTP` wraps the whole mux in the auth handler — never mount the SPA on a second unauthenticated server. `sse.StaticHandler` serves real files with correct Content-Type and falls any unknown path back to index.html for deep links.

Handoff to the real SPA build (next stage):

- Create the npm/bun web root (cc-present precedent: top-level `web/`, which in this repo family is always the JS workspace, never a Go package).
- Vite config sets `outDir: '../internal/web/dist'` with `emptyOutDir: true` and `base: '/'` (absolute asset URLs so deep links load).
- `vite build` replaces the placeholder index.html with the built one plus hashed assets; the gitignore rules keep everything but index.html untracked.

Before removing the placeholder or changing the flow, understand the tradeoff: no placeholder → clean-tree builds break; committing built artifacts → churn and merge noise in the tree.
ops.when: When modifying the web build process, considering the placeholder approach, or integrating a real web build into the pipeline
